observations: Photo 0 shows a large, dirty transmission assembly with a central black box labeled 'Lexus' and 'LS460'.
Photo 1 shows the same assembly from a different angle, with a person in an orange shirt visible.
The engine block is heavily soiled with dirt and grime.
The transmission casing is visible at the bottom right of photo 1.
No brand or model name is legible on the engine or transmission in either photo.

claims.evidence: The box in photo 0 and photo 1 clearly reads 'LS460'.
The engine is not a Lexus engine; it is a generic transmission.

claims.claim: Tokunbo, direct from Belgium. Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The item may not be a genuine Lexus LS460 transmission.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's identification plate (usually on the transmission casing).

risks.risk: The transmission may be seized, leaking, or have internal damage.
risks.proof: A video of the transmission being shifted through all gears.

risks.risk: The seller may be selling a used transmission from a different brand or model.
risks.proof: A photo of the transmission's identification plate.

proof_requests: Close-up of any label, sticker or metal plate showing the brand and model.
Photo of the transmission's identification plate showing the brand and model.
Video of the transmission being shifted through all gears to check for play or leaks.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
